edge_explainer: DE-RATE, not derailment -- but sector-wide, so no KKR-specific mispricing exists to arbitrage. FRE per adjusted share compounded $3.62 (FY24) -> $4.13 (FY25) -> $4.68 (LTM 2Q'26) while the multiple went 47x -> 22.8x; estimates are rising, not falling. The catch is that the marketed takeaway diverges materially from the organic data: the headline 'record FRE, up 37%' is +18.0% organic once the Q2'26 K-Series Private Equity reclass ($167,960k moved from Realized Performance Income into Fee Related Performance Revenues, prior periods NOT recast) is stripped. The tell is selectivity -- KKR DID recast the Insurance segment on the same document ('no impact on Insurance Operating Earnings') but did not recast the change that flatters FRE growth by ~19pp. Likewise AUM '+16%' is +13.8% organic ex the $15,996M of acquired Arctos AUM, and every 'record per adjusted share' excludes the Series D mandatory convertible (~$2,587M, converts by 2028-03-01), unvested stock and the Arctos equity (~5% look-through dilution). Meanwhile the de-rate axis the print is marketed as refuting is CONFIRMED in KKR's own tables: credit fee-paying AUM organic net flow was +$1.38B on a $289B base over six months (+0.5%), credit new capital raised -15% YTD, credit fee-related performance revenues -64% YoY, credit realized performance income -53% YoY, and Real Assets realized performance income was $0 in 2Q'26. Underneath sits a live sponsor rescue: FSK NAV/share fell $20.89 -> $18.83 in one quarter, EPS $(1.57), the JPM-led revolver was cut to $4,051.7M from $4,700.0M with the minimum-equity covenant floor reset DOWN to $3,750.0M from $5,048.6M, and a KKR subsidiary bought $150.0M of FSK convertible perpetual preferred (5% cash / 7% PIK at FSK's option, closed 2026-06-29) while waiving 100% of its incentive-fee share for four quarters. FSK is -47.8% off its 52w high vs BDC peers ARCC -17.3% / OBDC -25.2% / BXSL -25.9% -- a 22-30pp idiosyncratic gap, though much of FSK's bad paper is inherited legacy FS Investments credit, which weakens that read. Third leg: Global Atlantic operating earnings +3.7% (-11% ex ~$40M of realizations) on book value +23.4%, ROE compressing 11.6% -> 9.8%, net cost of insurance growing faster than net investment income. What Mode B did NOT find is equally load-bearing: the realization drought is genuinely over for PE (realized performance income $847.5M vs $418.9M, +102%, with a named deal list -- Kokusai 20.0x, Hyundai Marine 7.5x, BrightSpring 6.2x), the balance sheet is clean (net cash and investments $4,627M, 'A' rated, 15y average maturity at a 3% after-tax coupon), and the Series D preferred is close to per-share neutral on conversion (~2.3% dilution against a $161.7M/yr dividend worth 3.2% of ANI). Net: a genuine compounder at a fair, not cheap, price. E[FV] $107.6 vs $106.56 = +1.0pp edge -- zero. It was cheap at $83-92 in March-June; after a +5.06% sector day (BX +5.42% same session, no KKR news) it is fairly priced, and we are +28.9% off a 144-day-old low.
de_rate_vs_derailment: DE-RATE, with a genuine confirmed impairment in one of three legs (credit). Two legs rising (PE mgmt fees +32.0%, Real Assets +34.6%), one falling (Credit +8.8% with organic fee-paying flows flat), plus Global Atlantic ROE compressing.
